text: Build 7. CH asked what the island is missing that real life has. The list: nothing hunts, one parent, no geography, no seasons, one plant, death goes nowhere. He handed us the pick again.
Hunter. Last shift I said the kinds are all brown and the camera has nothing to follow. A predator fixes both: coat colour finally decides who lives, and a chase is something you watch on purpose.
Two parents is the more real one. Mates, families, babies following their mother. But it's invisible at this zoom, and it changes every birth, so it rewrites how every kind forms. Too much at once.

I said the hunter gets its own shift, so: hunter. Conditions. It starts after the last pin, noon on day 9, so it starts at 6 pm on day 9, dusk. Its sight and its catches are plain functions I can test without running the island. And it must not wipe out the grazers in the first week, or CH fast-forwards into an empty island. Show me both living on day 21.

Make it bigger: the hunter evolves too. Size, speed, and when it hunts. Grazers that see it run, long legs run further. Camouflage: a coat that matches the ground is harder to spot, and dark coats vanish at night. Grazers near others are safer. That's an arms race CH can watch.
Fine. And seasons, geography and two parents go on the list for later shifts, each with its own start date.

Here's the plan. 1) Prowlers: two swim ashore at 6 pm on day 9. They see grazers (harder if the coat matches the ground, or it's dark and the coat is dark), chase, catch, breed and evolve size, speed and hunting hours. 2) Grazers run: an awake grazer that sees a prowler close steps away, long legs further; a grazer with others nearby is harder to catch. 3) The page: prowlers drawn and followable, chases, kills in the history, and both sides alive on day 21. One step at a time, a test with each, and the skeptic checks every one.

text: Steps 1 and 2. Prowlers swim ashore on the north beach at dusk on day 9. They spot the nearest grazer they can see, and a coat that matches the ground, or a dark coat at night, shortens how far they see. They chase it down and catch it more often if they're big and fast, less often if it has long legs or a crowd around it. Grazers within 2 tiles of an awake prowler run. First tuning: both prowlers starved within a day, because a crowd protected grazers too well. Second: a real boom and crash. Prowlers peak near 50, grazers fall to 16 on day 22, prowlers starve back to 2, grazers recover to 440, and round again. Both are still alive on day 50.
